title: Windows Subsystem for Linux Launcher Activity
exclusions: Reports Sysmon Process Create events for an image whose basename is exactly `wsl.exe`. It does not prove malicious use, bypass, WSL installation, a running distribution, command success, Linux process execution details, network activity inside WSL 2, file access, distribution identity when absent from the command line, or policy violation. Microsoft documents `wsl.exe` as both the management and execution entry point, so bare and administrative invocations are retained. `wslservice.exe`, `wslconfig.exe`, `wslg.exe`, legacy `bash.exe`, distribution launchers, Linux processes inside WSL, and Windows child processes spawned from WSL require separate analytics. The `wineventlog` index is local. No automatic disablement, containment, runtime validation, or compliance assurance is claimed.
evidence: Retain `windows_wsl_launcher_activity` definition, ACL, schedule and results; Sysmon configuration hash/source health; each raw Event ID 1 with endpoint, user, integrity, image, command line, hashes, process/parent GUIDs and IDs, parent command, EventRecordID and time; WSL/Intune policy and approved-host inventory; distribution/version inventory where separately collected; related endpoint/network evidence; dated controls; analyst disposition; alert delivery; and bounded exceptions. This documentation-only review launched no WSL process and generated no event, search, alert, or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index, ingest Sysmon Event ID 1 with `Image=C:\\Windows\\System32\\wsl.exe`, `CommandLine=wsl.exe --distribution Ubuntu --exec /usr/bin/id`, `User=EXAMPLE\\alice`, `IntegrityLevel=Medium`, `ProcessGuid={11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111}`, `ParentImage=C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe`, `Computer=CLIENT01`, and `EventRecordID=94001`. Expect one row with `invocation_type=explicit_linux_command` and all raw process evidence preserved.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for `wslservice.exe`, `wslconfig.exe`, an unrelated `wsl.exe` string only in another process command line, Sysmon Event ID 5 for wsl.exe, Event ID 1 from another channel, and a qualifying image with empty endpoint. Ingest bare `wsl.exe` Event ID 1 and expect one `interactive_or_default_command` row rather than suppression.

dataSources: Microsoft Sysmon Process Create Event ID 1 from `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`, collected as XML with Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) into deployment-local `index=wineventlog`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`. Required fields are `Computer`, `EventRecordID`, `ProcessGuid`, `ProcessId`, `Image`, `CommandLine`, `CurrentDirectory`, `User`, `LogonGuid`, `LogonId`, `TerminalSessionId`, `IntegrityLevel`, `Hashes`, `ParentProcessGuid`, `ParentProcessId`, `ParentImage`, `ParentCommandLine`, `RuleName`, and event ID. Separate Intune/WSL inventory is needed to judge policy.
app: Microsoft Sysmon plus Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742), version 10.0.1. Microsoft Intune and Defender for Endpoint are optional policy/WSL visibility sources.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 earliest=-10m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval event_code=tonumber(coalesce(EventCode,EventID)), endpoint=lower(trim(coalesce(Computer,host))), process_image=lower(trim(Image)), process_name=replace(process_image,"^.*\\\\",""), command_line=lower(trim(CommandLine))
| where event_code=1 AND process_name="wsl.exe" AND len(endpoint)>0
| eval invocation_type=case(match(command_line,"(?i)(^|\s)(--exec|-e)(\s|$)"),"explicit_linux_command",match(command_line,"(?i)(^|\s)(--install|--unregister|--import|--import-in-place|--export|--update|--set-default|--set-default-version|--set-version|--mount|--unmount|--shutdown)(\s|$)"),"management_command",match(command_line,"(?i)(^|\s)(--system|--debug-shell|--user\s+root|-u\s+root)(\s|$)"),"privileged_or_debug_option",true(),"interactive_or_default_command"), use_case="UC-1.2.94"
| table _time endpoint invocation_type User IntegrityLevel Image CommandLine ProcessGuid ProcessId Hashes ParentImage ParentCommandLine ParentProcessGuid ParentProcessId CurrentDirectory LogonGuid LogonId TerminalSessionId EventRecordID RuleName source sourcetype use_case
| sort 0 -_time endpoint
description: Returns one Sysmon process-creation row for every exact `wsl.exe` launcher invocation and classifies its observed command line as explicit Linux command, management command, privileged/debug option, or interactive/default invocation. It preserves process and parent evidence without claiming the Linux command succeeded or was malicious.
value: WSL is legitimate enterprise and developer tooling, but it also provides a path to execute Linux commands from Windows and can create monitoring gaps when unmanaged. A complete launcher trail lets teams enforce server/workstation policy, understand normal development automation, and investigate unusual parent, user, option, or command context without treating all WSL use as an attack.
implementation: Deploy governed Sysmon ProcessCreate collection with command lines and hashes, collect the Operational channel as XML, and maintain an approved WSL host/policy inventory. Save the SPL as `windows_wsl_launcher_activity`, schedule every five minutes over the closed delayed bucket, and retain every invocation. Apply alert policy by asset role and context—for example any invocation on a server where Intune `AllowWSL` is disabled—then correlate Defender/WSL/network telemetry before response.
visualization: Restricted `Windows — WSL Activity` dashboard: Sysmon and WSL-policy coverage first; invocations by endpoint, user, parent image, and type; first-seen WSL hosts; management/privileged-option table; and complete process details. Drill down by ProcessGuid to parent/child, file, network, and EDR evidence and to Intune WSL policy/inventory. Missing launcher events or policy data must be unknown, not compliant.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Processes.process) as command_lines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process_names values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_commands values(Processes.process_id) as process_ids from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="wsl.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user
| rename Processes.* as *
schema: Microsoft Sysmon Event ID 1 native XML; optional Endpoint.Processes normalization
dataModelAcceleration: The optional Endpoint.Processes inventory is valid only after confirming `process_name=wsl.exe`, full command line in `process`, destination, user, parent and process ID mappings. It does not preserve ProcessGuid, hashes, integrity, EventRecordID, or every invocation row; raw XML remains authoritative.

knownFalsePositives:
A result is a real launcher event; the following common uses can resemble a suspicious command wrapper.

1. **Developer interactive shell or Linux build/test command** — Confirm approved WSL endpoint, user/team, distribution, repository/build job, parent terminal/IDE, and expected command. Retain audit history; use `windows_wsl_activity_exceptions.csv` only for a named automation pattern and expiry.

2. **Visual Studio Code Remote - WSL** — Verify signed VS Code path, Remote WSL extension, parent command, distribution, user session, and workspace. Helper/kill commands can use `-e`; scope notification suppression to exact signed parent/hash and managed developer assets.

3. **Docker Desktop WSL 2 backend** — Match signed Docker process chain, managed Docker configuration, `docker-desktop` distribution context, endpoint role, and update window. Do not allowlist all wsl.exe because the same host supports interactive use.

4. **IT deployment installing, updating, importing, exporting, or shutting down WSL** — Confirm Intune/software-deployment job, command, package/image hash, target ring, operator/service account, and UTC window. Management commands outside that job remain reviewable.

5. **Security engineering, malware-analysis, or purple-team use** — Verify isolated lab or authorized engagement, operator, distribution/image, command/timebox, and network controls. Preserve results as evidence and suppress only duplicate notification.

The post-result lookup requires exact endpoint or governed developer group, user/service identity, invocation type, approved parent/hash or command pattern, owner, reason, ticket, numeric start, and exclusive expiry. Reject global wsl.exe, all developers, all Docker parents, and open-ended entries.
hardware: Windows endpoints or servers capable of running WSL. WSL 2 Linux VM/distributions, Intune policy, Defender WSL telemetry, and internal Linux audit data are separate sources.
reviewer: documentation-only Cursor AI editorial review against Microsoft WSL architecture/commands/enterprise policy, Sysmon, Splunk Windows add-on/CIM, and MITRE ATT&CK; WSL installation, policy state, process fields, SPL, controls, source health, alerting, and Linux-side visibility were specified but not executed or Microsoft/WSL/Splunk/endpoint-SME signed

cost.search_load_notes: The wsl.exe filter is narrow, but Sysmon ProcessCreate is high-volume and must be sized across the endpoint fleet.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and exact launcher contract

Assign endpoint/WSL, Intune, developer-platform, Splunk, and security owners. Inventory where WSL is allowed, prohibited, or managed; approved distributions; WSL 1/2 policy; Docker/VS Code dependencies; and sensitive server roles. Install Sysmon and Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows 10.0.1 on required tiers. Restrict command/hash/user data.

Microsoft documents `wsl.exe` as the Windows entry point for executing Linux commands and managing distributions. `wslservice.exe` manages the WSL VM/distributions but is outside this launcher rule. The four invocation labels are triage helpers, not severity: `--exec/-e`, management options, privileged/debug options, or all other/bare commands.

## Step 1 — Collect Sysmon and policy context

Enable Sysmon ProcessCreate Event ID 1 with command line, hashes, parent and process GUIDs in a signed configuration. Record Event ID 16/configuration hash and measure volume. Collect **Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > Sysmon > Operational** as XML through an app-owned `inputs.conf` stanza to local `index=wineventlog`. Verify `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, exact source, and every required field against Event Viewer XML. Operate source health per endpoint.

In Microsoft Intune admin center use **Devices > Configuration Profiles > Settings catalog** and govern `AllowWSL`, `AllowInboxWSL`, `AllowWSL1`, debug-shell, networking, mount, and command settings appropriate to the environment. Export effective policy/inventory separately; process telemetry cannot prove policy state.

## Step 2 — Save and understand the report

Save as `windows_wsl_launcher_activity`, schedule every five minutes over `earliest=-10m@m latest=-5m@m`, and retain all rows. The base search fixes Sysmon channel/Event ID, derives image basename, and requires exact `wsl.exe`; command strings in other processes do not match. Ordered classification first identifies explicit execution, then management, then privileged/debug options, otherwise interactive/default use. Because a command may contain multiple categories, raw CommandLine remains authoritative.

Build alert policy after enrichment: any launcher on prohibited servers; first-seen host/user; unusual parent; root/debug/mount options; or commands inconsistent with developer automation. Keep base rows even when a post-result exception suppresses paging.

## Step 3 — Validate process semantics and policy

Run exact positive and negative fixtures with fixed bounds. Test System32 and Store/package paths, case, quoting, `-e`, `--exec`, management options, `--system`, `--debug-shell`, `-u root`, bare invocation, wrong executable/event/channel, and empty command. Verify ProcessGuid, parent and hashes. Do not require wslhost/wslservice child behavior for this report.

On an approved lab/developer endpoint, run harmless commands such as `wsl.exe --list --verbose` and `wsl.exe --distribution <lab> --exec /usr/bin/id`; compare Event Viewer XML, Splunk rows, Intune effective policy, and distribution inventory. Record versions, exact bounds, expected/actual rows, operator, alert delivery, and exception expiry.

## Step 4 — Operationalize investigation and response

For a review row: verify raw process/source health; validate image path/hash/signature and parent; check endpoint WSL policy and approved role; inspect user, integrity, command and distribution; correlate Windows process/network/file telemetry and Defender WSL/Linux visibility where deployed; contact owner; and determine whether the command is normal automation, policy drift, or suspicious execution.

Do not automatically unregister a distribution, run `wsl --shutdown`, disable WSL, delete VHDX files, isolate a developer workstation, or block a user solely from a launcher event. Those actions can destroy work or disrupt Docker/build systems. Use governed incident and endpoint-management procedures.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- **No wsl.exe events:** verify Sysmon ProcessCreate configuration, channel input, command-line fields, source health, image path, and schedule delay.
- **Linux command not visible:** confirm it appears in Windows `CommandLine`; interactive commands entered after bare wsl launch need Linux-side audit/Defender telemetry.
- **Docker or VS Code noise:** validate signed parent/hash and managed asset context, then apply a narrow expiring post-result lookup.
- **WSL prohibited but events appear:** confirm effective Intune assignment, Store versus inbox policy, user/device scope, sync state, and whether the event preceded enforcement.
- **CIM inventory differs:** inspect Endpoint.Processes process/process_name mappings and acceleration freshness; raw XML is authority.
- **Renamed or distribution launcher missed:** explicit exclusion; add a separately sourced analytic rather than broad `*wsl*` matching.
- **Duplicate events:** compare Computer, EventRecordID, ProcessGuid, and direct/WEF collection paths and repair topology.
grandmaExplanation: We keep a record whenever someone starts the Linux environment built into Windows. It is useful and often approved, but the record helps the team spot it on computers where it is not allowed and review unusual commands without blaming every developer.
